title: Runoff at equal rain did not fall in the 2010-2019 central-Chile megadrought (64 near-natural catchments) but fell 19% in south-east Australia in 1997-2003 with the same linear annual method
abstract: Question: is the persistent south-east Australian (SE-AU) runoff deficit at equal rain a general result of a long drought with a known climatic driver? Central Chile has the same Mediterranean winter-rain climate and the same driver (poleward shift of the westerlies), and a deeper drought from 2010. Method: for 64 near-natural CAMELS-CL catchments (30-42 S) and 260 CAMELS-AUS catchments (VIC, NSW, ACT), we fitted annual Q = a + bP + cP(t-1) on the pre-drought years and calculated the departure of a 7-year drought window. Leave-window-out departures of all earlier 7-year windows gave the null. Chilean rain was CR2MET v2.5 (1960-2021), with checks from CR2MET v1, a 1979 baseline and a fixed index of 135 rain gauges. Result: the Chilean median departure was -2.6% in 2010-2016 (95% year bootstrap -10.3 to +5.7) and -0.4% in 2010-2019, inside the earlier range (-9% to +10%); 6% of catchments were below all their earlier windows (4% by chance). With the same method, SE-AU lost 19.1% in 1997-2003 (-31.2 to -12.5) and 20.1% in 2010-2016, below the earlier range, with 47% of catchments below all earlier windows. At matched runoff ratio and rain deficit, 80% of Chilean catchments had a smaller deficit than their SE-AU matches. Southern Chile (35-42 S) stayed near zero with all rain sources (-3% to +2%). Northern, snow-influenced Chile depends on the rain source (-26% to +12%), so we make no conclusion there. A linear rain-sensitivity-loss statistic was similar in both regions but changed sign with square-root or log models, so it does not separate them. Conclusion: a long, deep drought with the same climatic driver is not sufficient to make the SE-AU deficit. Limits: Chilean flows end in water year 2019 (the 2023 wet year is not tested), fewer Chilean catchments, short overlap in runoff ratio.

display.caption: Regional median runoff departure from the pre-drought rain-runoff fit for earlier 7-year windows (line, left out of the fit) and the drought window (point, 95% year bootstrap). Chile 2010-2016 stays inside its earlier range; SE Australia 1997-2003 and 2010-2016 fall below it.
Drought-window departure of each catchment against its baseline runoff ratio. At equal runoff ratio, Chilean departures are near zero and SE-Australian departures are mostly negative.
Median departure for different rain sources, baselines and model forms. Southern Chile is near zero in all cases; northern Chile depends on the rain source; SE Australia stays below zero.
